questions.q: Why does `server_name = "web-01"` fail in a Bash script?
options: Spaces around the = cause Bash to parse it as a command named server_name with arguments
Variables must be declared with a type first
Double quotes aren't allowed in assignments
questions.explain: Bash assignment syntax requires no spaces around =. With spaces, Bash treats server_name as a command and = and "web-01" as its arguments.

questions.q: What's the main practical advantage of `[[ ]]` over `[ ]` for a test?
options: [[ ]] doesn't word-split or glob-expand unquoted variables, and supports && / || directly inside it
[ ] is deprecated and no longer works in Bash
[[ ]] can only be used outside of if statements
questions.explain: [[ ]] is Bash's extended test syntax: it's more forgiving with unquoted variables and lets you combine conditions with && / || inside the brackets.

questions.q: Which operator correctly compares two numbers for equality in a test?
questions.explain: -eq (along with -ne, -lt, -le, -gt, -ge) is for numeric comparison. == and != are for comparing strings.

options: Always prints 'directory exists' regardless of the test result
Prints 'directory exists' only if $backup_dir is a directory that exists, since && only runs on success
Creates the directory if it doesn't exist
Deletes the directory if it exists
questions.explain: -d tests whether the path is an existing directory. && only runs the command on its right if the test on its left succeeded (exit status 0).

questions.q: In an if/elif/else block, what keyword must appear at the end to close it?
questions.explain: Bash closes an if block with fi (if spelled backward). done closes loops, not if blocks.
